title: People Operations Associate (AI and Automation)
description: Hi, I’m Ellie, People Lead at hx. I joined hx in January 2025 as a Senior People Partner and have recently stepped into the People Lead role. Outside of work, I’m an F1 fan and dog mum, so I’m no stranger to fast-paced environments or the occasional pit stop for walkies. Our People team supports all things people at hx, from performance and engagement to the systems, insights and day-to-day operations that help our teams do their best work. We’re growing the team and looking for someone to own our People reporting and analytics, while helping keep the operational side of the function running smoothly. It’s a great opportunity for someone who enjoys turning data into meaningful insights, wants to make a real impact and is excited to help shape how the People team grows alongside the business. Interested? Read more about the role and life at hx below. About hyperexponential (hx) At hyperexponential, we're building the AI-powered platform that enables the world's most critical decisions in a $7 trillion industry, which risks to take, and how to price them. These are the decisions that shape real-world outcomes: whether rockets successfully launch into space, autonomous vehicles make it to market, or communities recover after major storms. Until now, insurance has been making billion-dollar decisions using outdated tools. We're changing that. Our platform brings together data, AI, and human expertise to give insurers the fastest path from submission to decision, helping them move faster, act smarter, and take on more risk with confidence. Backed by a16z, Highland Europe, and Battery Ventures, we're scaling globally, already trusted by nearly 50 of the world's largest insurers, with zero churn and billions in premiums flowing through hx. What began as a single product in one market has rapidly evolved into a multi-product, multi-territory platform powering every stage of pricing and underwriting. AI is at the core of what we do, from building the world's first domain-specific AI peer programmer for insurance (think GitHub Copilot with a PhD in actuarial science) to shaping agentic workflows that reinvent how this industry operates. What makes hx different is the people who build it. Here, impact isn't tied to title or tenure, it's defined by the challenges you take on and the discipline you bring. Surrounded by peers who stretch you, you'll do the best, hardest work of your life in a company engineered to endure. If that sounds like you, join us in building what comes next. About the People team Our People team owns the systems and data that keep hx a high-performance, high-engagement place to work: performance and growth, people analytics, compensation and benefits, and HR compliance. We are building the reporting layer that lets the business make faster, better-evidenced decisions about its people rather than relying on instinct, and we work closely with Talent to connect hiring and pipeline data with performance and engagement data so leaders see the full employee lifecycle instead of fragments of it. Inside People and Talent, AI has already changed how we screen, how we write up interviews and how we surface insight to leaders. There is far more to do. Plenty of what we do still runs on manual effort that could be designed out, and this role exists to go after that. We care much more about what you have built and put in front of real users than about the size of the team you have sat in, and impact here isn't tied to title or tenure. You will work directly with People Leaders, with real scope to shape how the team works as we grow. One thing worth being direct about: there is no finished playbook here. If you need a well-defined remit and clear instruction to do your best work, this will be frustrating. If you would rather find the problem yourself and build the fix, you will have a lot of room.. What you'll be doing Build the AI tooling that our People and Talent function runs on. Agents that answer the questions currently landing in our inbox, skills that draft the documents we write manually, workflows that pull our systems together. This is the core of the role rather than a project on the side. Build out the People reporting layer, including dashboards on retention, attrition and engagement, and get to the point where you can tell us what the numbers mean, not just what they are. Work with Talent to connect hiring and pipeline data to People data, and make that view something leaders can interrogate themselves. Learn our people processes properly, starting with onboarding, payroll data integrity and the performance cycle, then rebuild the parts that depend on manual effort. Support our performance review cycles in Lattice and our engagement surveys, help analyse what comes out of them, and automate the parts that should not need a person. Help keep our HRIS data accurate, including records, reporting and system troubleshooting. What you'll need to have done Built and shipped something with AI that other people used, whether that is an agent, a script, a tool, a bot or a side project. Got past the first version. We will ask how you tested it, what it got wrong with real users and what you changed as a result. If you have a long list of things you have experimented with, we want to hear what each one taught you. Worked with more than one model or platform, and formed a view on what each is good for. Worked with a real dataset, cleaned it up, and drawn a conclusion you could defend. Been responsible for keeping a system or record accurate, whether that is a tracker, a membership list, a codebase or admin for a part-time role. Handled something that needed to stay confidential, or can show us how you think about handling sensitive information. Genuine interest in how organisations work, and the willingness to learn a domain where the detail matters and the consequences of getting it wrong land on real colleagues. How we build in an AI-forward company hx is a maximally AI-forward company because we believe AI should amplify what exceptional people can achieve. Everyone here is a builder. That means staying close to what’s changing, continuing to learn, and using AI to raise the quality, pace and ambition of your work. We expect everyone to actively experiment with AI and agentic systems, whether at work or in their personal lives. This means going beyond prompting, exploring what agents can do autonomously, and learning by doing. You don't need to be an engineer, but you do need to be curious, hands-on and willing to push what's possible. Your current environment is context, not the answer. We’re interested in how you think about what should be possible now, not simply how things are done where you work today. We care about judgement, creativity and ownership, not simply using more tools. The bar is simple: your work should be meaningfully better because of how you operate in this new world. Compensation This role sits within a £40,000 - £55,000 salary range. At hx, we're committed to salary transparency, you'll always have clarity on pay early in the process, and our Talent Partner will share more detail with you during initial conversations. We're also working towards publishing salary information for all roles globally. Because we're building at the intersection of technology/SaaS and insurance, our roles don't always map neatly onto traditional benchmarks. Our approach is to design compensation that's competitive in the market, fair across teams, and aligned with the impact our people make. Benefits £5,000 training and conference budget for individual and group development. 25 days of holiday plus 8 bank holidays (33 days total). Company pension scheme via Penfold. Mental health support and therapy via Spectrum.life . Individual wellbeing allowance via Juno. Private healthcare insurance through AXA. Income protection and Life Insurance. Cycle to Work Scheme. Additional perks Top-spec equipment (laptop, screens, adjustable desks, etc.). Regular remote and in-person hackathons, lunch and learns, socials, and games nights. Team breakfasts and lunches, snacks, drinks fridge, and a fun office at The Ministry. Exceptional opportunities for personal development and growth as we build something remarkable together. Interview process Initial call with our Talent team to kick things off and learn more about your background. Manager interview with our People Lead to explore your experience in more depth. Skills assessment, presenting a People Analytics deliverable to the team. Values interview to get to know how you work and how that aligns with hx's culture with our VP of People and Senior Director of Finance and Operations. We know that progress depends on diverse perspectives, and we are committed to creating an environment where everyone can thrive, grow, and make an impact. We recognise there is always more to do, and we take responsibility for shaping a workplace that is not only diverse but genuinely inclusive. Diversity is not just the right thing to do, it is key to solving the complex challenges we choose to take on. By welcoming people from all backgrounds and experiences, we strengthen our ability to question assumptions, push boundaries, and design solutions that endure. If you're energised by complexity and motivated to grow, we encourage you to apply and join our global team. description: About the Team OpenAI’s Forward Deployed Engineering team builds with customers to bring frontier AI into production. Our Cyber FDEs partner with the security and engineering teams that defend globally critical systems, from enterprise software to the core infrastructure it runs on. Cyber FDEs work closely with our Product, Research, and Go-to-Market teams to adapt our products and models to what customers need to defend their systems. About the Role You’ll build systems that give defenders an advantage at a scale few engineering teams encounter. You might help an enterprise identify, test, and deploy patches across hundreds of thousands of code repositories, or help a security team analyze petabytes of logs for signs of malicious agents or coordinated attacks. Across these deployments, you’ll build tools that customer engineers can trust to support consequential security decisions. You’ll work directly with customer security teams, from CISOs to frontline analysts. As AI changes how attackers operate, you’ll help these teams determine where their defenses need to evolve, prioritize what to build, and validate solutions with the engineers who will operate them. Alongside OpenAI’s account teams, you’ll translate security priorities into deployed systems that help defenders cover more ground. You’ll also help shape what OpenAI builds next. When you identify a gap between what defenders need and what today’s models or products can do, you’ll partner with Research and Product to define, build, and test capabilities that address it. This role is based in London. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week. We offer relocation assistance. Travel up to 50% is required. In this role you will: Partner with customer security leaders and OpenAI’s Go-to-Market team to scope engagements, establish responsibilities, and define measurable success criteria. Lead technical design and implementation alongside customer engineers. Integrate agents into security workflows, establish access boundaries, and determine which actions require human review. Build evaluations grounded in the decisions defenders make. For a patching agent, test whether a fix blocks a known exploit while preserving expected application behavior. For a detection system, replay historical attacks alongside normal traffic to measure detection speed and false-positive rates. Guide production rollout with the engineers who will operate the system. Provide the observability and controls they need to understand system behavior, intervene when necessary, and expand adoption with confidence. Translate successful approaches across deployments into reusable tools and engineering practices that other defenders can adopt. You might thrive in this role if you: 5+ years of software engineering experience, including building and shipping production software. Experience protecting production systems through work in security engineering, infrastructure, SRE, DevOps, or product engineering. Experience building and evaluating AI agents for software engineering workflows. Experience with CI/CD pipelines and practices that maintain code quality, reliability, and security. Ability to navigate unfamiliar codebases and contribute maintainable, production-quality changes. Ability to communicate technical concepts and trade-offs to engineering teams and senior security stakeholders. Additional experience includes: Cybersecurity spans many disciplines, and while we’re primarily looking for strong engineering generalists, we’d love to hear about deeper experience in any of the following areas: Security curiosity and experimentation: You read CVE write-ups because you want to understand how things break. You may have built an agent honeypot to test a hypothesis—or prove a point—and enjoy turning a security question into a hands-on experiment. Security community engagement: You enjoy exchanging ideas with defenders, whether that’s discussing security strategy with a CISO at Black Hat or comparing technical approaches with frontline practitioners. Application security: You’ve written CodeQL queries or Semgrep rules, built fuzzing harnesses, or discovered and responsibly disclosed vulnerabilities. We operate at the intersection of field delivery and internal development, working closely with Product, Research, and Go-To-Market (GTM). About the role As a foundational FDE manager, you’ll lead FDE through high-stakes, ambiguous customer deployments and own technical and business value outcomes end to end. You’ll grow a team that can operate under pressure and help OpenAI learn from the field. You’ll partner closely with Product, Research, Sales, and GTM to ensure fieldwork informs roadmap priorities, drives new exploration, and supports safe deployment at scale. Your decisions will influence how OpenAI is trusted by the customers closest to our deployment work. Your success will be measured by how consistently your team ships, how clearly you deliver signal to Research and Product, and how durable your team and delivery model prove to be. This role is based in London. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees. This role also will require travel up to 25%. In this role you will Lead and grow a team of FDE delivering production systems with frontier models Own end-to-end delivery outcomes through clarity, speed, tight coordination, and technical quality Codify what works into tools, playbooks, and roadmap inputs that create leverage for both OpenAI and our wider developer community Notice early indicators and raise them with urgency, whether in product behavior, customer environments, or delivery practices Use judgement to distinguish what requires action and what does not Set a high bar for FDE performance and support each person’s growth through direct, actionable feedback Define how we staff and support field teams that can scale without added complexity You might thrive in this role if you Bring 8+ years of engineering or technical delivery experience, including 2+ years managing high-performing FDE or customer-facing engineers Have led high-pressure technical projects from prototype to production Write and review production-grade code across frontend and backend using Javascript or Python Simplify complex work and make fast, sound decisions under pressure Elevate team performance through clarity, not process Operate with urgency in ambiguous or evolving environments Translate field experience into sharp, actionable feedback for Product and Research Build deep trust with your team by modeling calm, focus, and judgment when it matters most About OpenAI OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. title: Account Executive
description: View our much better version of this job spec on our careers page: https://juro.notion.site/ae *** THE KEY BITS Location : We can currently only accept applications from candidates that are located and have long-term working rights in the UK. Flexibility : We have office hubs in London and Boston, plus remote teams across several European countries. Under our choice-first work approach, you can work fully remotely from Day 1. That said, we’ve found people generally ramp faster when they spend a few days a week in the office alongside the team (esp. in the early months) and we hope you’ll want to. Salary : We benchmarked £62-70k base + 100% variable (OTE £124-140k) with accelerators, at IC3 level in our progression framework for someone based in the UK. Interviews : 3 stages totalling around 3 hours over about 3 weeks. Start date : As soon as you can start. Reporting to : Max Baldry-Steen, Director of Sales More info : The FAQ below, juro.com/careers , our handbook or ask ----- anything. HELP US HELP THE WORLD AGREE FASTER Juro has big ambitions: to make it incredibly easy for anyone to agree and manage legal contracts. And we'll need help doing it . Legal tech is on the rise, with Goldman Sachs estimating that 44% of legal tasks can be automated with generative AI. With the brand we have built and the agility of early stage we are well placed to capture this opportunity. Buyers come to Juro because we're easy to use and fast to implement, AI runs through the whole product and our product team ships fast. To keep up with that demand in 2027, we're growing our Account Executive team. Your role is to drive new business growth at Juro. That means: Meet or beat your ARR target (around $800k new business a year). Build a strong pipeline, with a good share of it from leads you generate yourself. Land a clear value narrative with prospects: real pain, a business case, buy-in from several stakeholders. Keep your CRM and forecast reliable and accurate. Run a high-velocity motion that makes it easy for smaller companies to buy Juro, alongside larger $100k+ deals. We care about building a diverse team where everyone feels they belong. That’s why our perks & benefits and choice-first work approach are designed with inclusivity in mind. Read more in our diversity, inclusion & belonging hub . WHO WE LOOK FOR Research shows that while men apply to jobs if they meet ~60% of criteria, women and those in traditionally under-represented groups tend to apply only if they check all boxes. So if you think you have what it takes but don't meet every single point above, please still get in touch. We'd love to have a chat and see if you could be a great fit. To succeed here: Every Juror finds their balance across our four Principles . We hire, develop and celebrate people who live them every day. Curious how you’d fit? Try our personality quiz to see how you map against our principles. On top of that, you have been part of a journey where: You carried and hit a quota of around $800k a year at a B2B SaaS scale-up, incl. a good share of pipeline you built yourself. You sold in a high-velocity motion - 5-week cycles and ACVs around $20-50k — you also closed some larger deals. You multi-thread by default, and your discovery builds a business case with several stakeholders, not a feature tour. You use AI every day in your sales work (research, call prep, follow-up) and have opinions about what works. This job likely isn’t for you if: Your quota, velocity or ACV are far from ours. Quotas under $600k, 90+ day cycles, or deals well outside $20-100k usually make ramping here hard. You’re waiting for marketing to fill your pipeline. Our inbound is strong, but the best reps here build their own. You rely on a single champion to carry the deal. You wait for the buyer to set next steps. Here, AEs ask for the deal and drive it. You don't want regular feedback. We share call scorecards and pipeline data openly, and we expect you to act on them quickly. Your pitch is "sales-y". We sell to legal and operations leaders, who dislike that style. OUR MISSION Juro exists to help the world agree faster by making it incredibly easy for anyone to agree and manage legal contracts. The load on legal teams is increasing as business teams move faster with the help of AI. The only way out is to deploy AI within the legal team so that (a) routine contract work can be executed autonomously and (b) lawyers’ time is reserved for problem solving. It’s like having an extra team member that is always on and takes on heavy lifting. Just like an in-house lawyer, Juro: is present for, and trusted by, business teams owns contracts from first draft to signature and beyond builds judgement from every contract it works on …all within guardrails controlled by the legal team. You’ll work across data, post-training, evals, and model behavior, taking ideas from failure analysis to production. If you want to shape model behavior at consumer scale, this is the role. title: Manager - Transaction Services
description: About Unity Advisory Unity Advisory is a modern advisory business built for today's CFO, with connected solutions across finance, deals and tax. Focussed on client outcomes, seasoned experts lead every engagement, in an operating model powered by AI and free from audit conflict. Unity Advisory is a new kind of partner for the office of the CFO. Founded by senior leaders from the world's top advisory firms and backed by Warburg Pincus, we provide integrated finance, commercial, tax and deals support: expert advice, sharper execution, and delivery models built around how organisations operate today. CFOs need trusted advisers without legacy complexity, so we pair expert human judgement with proprietary AI workflows and smart automation, free from audit conflicts. The Role We built our deals practice around the client's decision: whether to buy, whether to sell, at what price, on what terms. We work alongside our clients rather than at arm's length, in the room while the deal decision is being made, and our support carries on beyond signing: into the 100-day plan, the hold period and the eventual exit. And that support draws on the whole firm: our tax, finance and commercial specialists work as one team with the deals practice, so the advice a client gets after signing is as integrated as the diligence that came before it. We're looking for a Manager to join our Financial Due Diligence team. You'll run buy-side and sell-side engagements day to day: getting into the numbers, managing the team on the ground, and making sure clients get clear, well-supported findings on time. You'll bring solid FDD or transaction services experience from a Big 4 or top-tier advisory firm, and own an engagement from scoping through to final findings. You'll work alongside our Partners and Directors and directly with clients and target company management from day one. This is a hybrid role based in our Mayfair office. title: Principal Compliance Officer
description: <div class="content-intro"><p>SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today, SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of making life multiplanetary and expanding consciousness to the stars.<br><br>SpaceXSI is building Super Intelligence to help humanity understand the universe. Our teams are building the full Super Intelligence stack: from our Colossus supercomputers, to Grok models, to our suite of applications, including Grok Bot, Grok Build, Grok Imagine, Grok Voice, and X. We're creating a powerful flywheel where more compute trains better models, better models power more useful products, and what we learn from people using those products shapes what we build next.</p></div><h4><strong>PRINCIPAL COMPLIANCE OFFICER</strong></h4> <p>The UK financial crime program is being built now, and it has to stand up to the FCA. This role sits in Compliance, reports to the US BSA/AML Officer, and owns the UK framework end to end — AML/CTF, sanctions, fraud, ABC, KYC/CDD/EDD, transaction monitoring, SARs, and the operating rhythm. You will still work the hard cases. It is a builder seat with accountability, not a queue job with “strategy” in the title.</p> <p>If you have eight or more years inside an FCA-regulated bank, EMI, PI, or payments firm, have owned or rebuilt a financial crime control framework, and can still open a file, this is the seat. You will build the UK program from the ground up, setting the standards the team and the FCA will use. This is consumer-scale payments financial crime work – not a private-banking book – and you’ll sit directly with Product and Engineering. You’ll operate in a small team with a direct line to the US BSA/AML Officer, where scope is broad and process is lean. The measure of success is a program that still works a year later, and the role sits alongside MLRO / SMF17-adjacent duties for the UK entity.</p> <h4><strong>RESPONSIBILITIES:</strong></h4> <ul> <li>Design and run the UK financial crime programme: policy, procedures, CDD/EDD, risk rating, sanctions screening, transaction monitoring, SAR handling, escalation, QA, and training</li> <li>Turn MLR 2017, POCA, the Sanctions and Anti-Money Laundering Act, JMLSG, the FCA Financial Crime Guide, SYSC 6.3, and payments/EMI expectations into something operations and product can run</li> <li>Own the UK business-wide risk assessment and keep it honest as the product, customer mix, and channels change</li> <li>Handle complex cases — PEPs, adverse media, sanctions hits, high-risk onboarding, fraud typologies, escalations — then use the queue to fix the framework</li> <li>Stand up first- and second-line controls: documentation, workflows, vendor oversight, quality sampling, MI, and issue management</li> <li>Put UK requirements into the customer journey with Legal, Operations, Product, and Engineering. Be the UK voice in global design decisions</li> <li>Report on quality, residual risk, throughput, and control health, and prepare the program for internal audit, skilled-person reviews, and FCA scrutiny</li> <li>Build the operating model as the team grows.</li> <li>Hire, coach, and set the standard</li> <li>Support MLRO / SMF17-adjacent duties as the UK permissions model requires</li> </ul> <h4><strong>BASiC QUALIFICATIONS:</strong></h4> <ul> <li>8+ years of hands-on experience with financial crime in a regulated UK firm (bank, EMI, PI, payments, or e-money), including substantial KYC/CDD/EDD</li> </ul> <h4><strong>PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:</strong></h4> <ul> <li>You will still do the cases, close gaps in a small team, do not wait for a 30-page RACI</li> <li>You know the UK regime well enough to argue a point — MLR 2017, JMLSG, POCA, UK sanctions, FCA expectations — and how it lands in a payments product</li> <li>You have designed or rebuilt a framework, procedure, or control, not only cleared files or written a policy nobody ran</li> <li>You have led people or a workstream. You can defend a risk decision and explain it to the Product without jargon</li> <li>EU financial crime experience</li> <li>Experience with the EU AML package, 6AMLD, EBA guidelines, national transposition, or an EU FIU/regulator, especially on cross-border payments, wallets, or EMI/PI products (useful because X Money will not stay inside one perimeter)</li> </ul> <h4><strong>ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:</strong></h4> <ul> <li>In-office five days a week; occasional work-from-home when needed</li> </ul> <h4><strong>COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS:</strong></h4> <ul> <li>Competitive base + equity</li> <li>UK private medical covering GPs and specialists; pension; life insurance</li> <li>25 days’ paid time off; lunch and dinner allowance</li> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><p><em>SpaceXSI is an equal opportunity employer. For details on data processing, view our </em><em><a href="https://x.ai/legal/recruitment-privacy-notice" target="_blank">Recruitment Privacy Notice</a>.</em></p></div> Find Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

title: VP of Engineering
description: We built ClearBank on the belief that banking infrastructure would no longer slow down progress. Instead, it would be a catalyst that unlocks the potential to innovate. It would adapt to different needs so a new era in financial services could begin. We’re here to challenge the status quo in banking, are you? We all know that transforming banking forever is not an easy mission, but we’re more than ready to rise to that challenge. We all do it every day; navigating new, unexpected and sometimes even daunting challenges. But we believe in ourselves and trust we can do it. Want to innovate? Go for it. Push for a better way? You Can. If you think you have it in you, this is Where You Can. About Us ClearBank is a technology‑enabled, fully regulated bank providing cloud‑based banking and payments infrastructure to financial institutions. We operate at scale in a highly regulated environment, where trust, resilience and security are critical. Our engineering organisation is focused on enabling frequent, reliable change while maintaining strong controls. We believe quality is not a gate at the end of delivery, but something designed in from the very start. Role Purpose This is a senior leadership role accountable for the strategy, design, build, operation and ongoing resilience of ClearBank’s payments and cards platforms. The VP of Payments & Cards will lead multiple engineering teams responsible for real-time, scheme-connected payments and cards systems across the UK, Europe, and future international markets. This requires deep experience working close to the infrastructure that moves money. Ideally, this will include direct integration with major payment schemes or rails, such as FPS, Bacs or CHAPS in the UK, SEPA payment schemes in Europe, or ACH and Fedwire in the US. We will also consider experience gained through payment infrastructure providers or connectivity platforms provided it includes sufficient technical depth in payment processing, scheme connectivity and the operation of highly available, regulated payments infrastructure. The role will define platform strategy, engineering standards, tooling and ways of working, while embedding a shift-left quality mindset across delivery. Success means delivering highly resilient, highly available, secure, scalable and compliant platforms that enable frequent, reliable change in a regulated banking environment. Key Responsibilities Own the strategy, design, build and run of real-time payments and cards platforms across the UK, Europe, the US and future international markets, including direct scheme connectivity and integrations with third-party payment infrastructure providers. Lead the delivery and operation of digital wallet capabilities, including Apple Pay and Google Pay implementations. Set the technical direction for payments and cards platforms, ensuring architectural choices support resilience, availability, scalability, performance, security and cost efficiency. Own the budget for the Payments and Cards engineering teams, ensuring effective investment in people, tooling and platforms. Build, lead and develop high-performing engineering teams, creating clear accountability, strong delivery discipline and a culture of engineering excellence. Ensure platforms are designed and operated to meet the following outcomes: Highly resilient — supporting local and cross-region disaster recovery requirements. Highly available — targeting 99.999% aggregate internal availability where appropriate. Highly scalable — supporting aggressive growth targets and future business volumes. Performant — meeting scheme performance requirements and exceeding client expectations on latency. Cost optimised — balancing client value, operational efficiency and ClearBank’s cost base. Establish scalable engineering quality standards, practices and governance across the payments and cards domain. Embed quality, observability, operational readiness and control requirements into delivery practices and CI/CD pipelines. Drive engineering productivity through AI-assisted and increasingly agentic software engineering, including the effective use of AI coding tools and multi-agent approaches across development, testing and engineering workflows, with appropriate risk, security and regulatory guardrails. Partner closely with the CTO, engineering leaders, product, risk, compliance and operations teams to ensure delivery decisions balance pace, quality and control. Ensure software development and platform operations meet regulatory, audit, resilience and compliance expectations. Skills & Experience Senior engineering leadership experience in payments, cards or highly regulated financial technology environments. Proven experience establishing, scaling and operating engineering teams, standards and practices. Direct experience integrating with, building against or operating connectivity to payment schemes or rails. Relevant examples include Faster Payments, Bacs or CHAPS in the UK; SEPA payment schemes and associated euro payment infrastructure in Europe; ACH or Fedwire in the US; or card networks and associated issuing or acquiring infrastructure. Alternatively, substantial experience delivering payment connectivity through a provider such as Form3 or an equivalent platform, with demonstrable technical depth in how payments are processed, routed and operated. Experience delivering or operating digital wallet capabilities, such as Apple Pay and Google Pay. Strong understanding of real-time, high-availability, high-throughput distributed systems. Strong background working in regulated environments, with practical experience of audit, compliance, operational resilience and control frameworks. Deep understanding of shift-left quality, test automation, modern quality engineering and secure software development practices. Experience using modern AI-enabled engineering tooling and a strong understanding of how agentic or multi-agent approaches can improve software development, testing and engineering delivery in a controlled and responsible way. Strong security mindset, with an appreciation of evolving threats, mitigations and secure platform design. Demonstrated ability to influence across multiple teams and senior stakeholders, including where direct line management is not present. Excellent collaboration and communication skills, with the ability to work effectively with engineering, product, risk, compliance and executive stakeholders. Sound judgement in balancing delivery pace, customer outcomes, regulatory expectations, operational risk and engineering quality. A little bit more about us! ClearBank is Where You Can belong: At ClearBank we think about Diversity, Equity and Inclusion (DE&I) a lot. Not because we think we should. But because we know we should – how else can we build a happy workforce and be successful as a business. We’re committed to making sure our teams reflect society. And we put energy and effort into making this a place where everyone feels at home, where they’re given the trust and encouragement to do their very best work. Here are some of the things we’re most proud of: 42% of our senior management roles are held by women Our enhanced family leave policies Launching our partnership with Code First Girls Increasing awareness of neurodiversity in the workplace through our partnership with the Inclusive Group Our hiring process and what you can expect: Application: a member of our talent acquisition team will review your application against the key requirements for the role and let you know within two weeks whether you’re moving forward to the next stage; Screening: You’ll spend 30-45 minutes speaking to one of our recruiters learning more about the role and ClearBank, and we’ll get it know more about you, your experience and how your skills align with the role (this will be via phone or Teams video call). You can expect to hear back from us within seven days following this meeting (if things are taking longer than expected, we’ll let you know that too); First Interview: You’ll spend one hour with a member of our hiring team focusing on your skills, competencies and your ways of working at the same time we’ll give you time to ask more questions about the role, the team and learn more about the ClearBank culture. This will be via Teams. Second Interview: This will be a competency-based interview with one or more members of our team. Final Stage: You will have a final meeting with the Head of Department. This will be around 45-60 minutes. Offer: Congratulations! Get ready to transform banking forever! Our commitment to you as a candidate: We will always try our best to get back to you within seven days of your interview whether you’ve been successful or not and provide you with feedback. Sometimes things take a little longer, so we may not have a decision to share but we will get it touch to let you know we need a little more time. We’re unable to provide specific individual feedback at the application or screening stage but know that your application was reviewed and considered carefully. We wish you the best of luck with your application and maybe we’ll be celebrating your new role at ClearBank soon! Equal Opportunities ClearBank is committed to ensuring equal opportunities throughout every stage of the recruitment process. ClearBank recognises that diversity is vital to the long-term success of the business in the communities and markets in which it operates. ClearBank is also a firm believer that an inclusive culture fosters greater employee engagement and collaboration. ClearBank strives for diversity and inclusion of all forms, including (but not limited to): gender, age, educational and professional background, disability, gender reassignment, marital or civil partner status, pregnancy or maternity, race, colour, nationality, ethnic or national origin, religion or belief and sexual orientation. As part of the Company’s commitment to equal employment opportunity, we provide reasonable adjustments, to candidates during the recruitment process, including to individuals with disabilities. We want to create a safe space that welcomes everyone so please let us know how we can accommodate you. In case you have any accessibility requirements you can share that with our Talent Acquisition team prior to your interview stage, if applicable. The legal bit By submitting your CV to ClearBank Limited you are providing your consent for us to use the information you provide for recruitment purposes. For more information on how we manage your data go and check out our Candidate Privacy Notice on the ClearBank website to see how we process, manage and look after your data. You are also allowing us to communicate with you by email and telephone for recruitment purposes. Find Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

title: Senior Product Manager, Data Foundry
description: ABOUT BEAMERY With the rapid expansion of AI and automation, the future of work has never been more challenging for organizations. Beamery’s unique jobs, skills and tasks data platform helps organizations navigate these challenges and make more informed decisions across Talent Lifecycle Management. Our solutions power recruitment, mobility, upskilling, diversity, work architecture and workforce planning for some of the world’s most forward-thinking companies. We believe that where you work is much more than just a job. Millions of people are being left behind every day in their careers, and we’re on a mission to fix this by creating equal access to meaningful work, skills and careers for all. We are an equal opportunity employer committed to building a representative Beamery, creating an equitable, inclusive and engaging environment for our people. So, what are you waiting for? Join us and help us transform the future of work once and for all. What’s ahead — and why it’s an exciting time to join the team: Building agentic AI with advanced orchestration (multi-agent workflows, tool use, evaluation loops) that turns complex talent data into decisions. Training and fine-tuning our own models on unique data about jobs, skills and tasks, and benchmarking them against the best in our market. Joining an award-winning AI team (ACM RecSys Challenge 2026) that turns new ideas into innovative solutions with scientific rigour. Sharing our work and learning from industry peers through challenges, conferences and publications. But it’s not all about creating high-quality products, we also very much value the company culture we have worked hard to create; built on trust, empathy & honesty ensuring our workforce is able to bring their full selves to work. About the opportunity at Beamery We are looking for an experienced Senior Product Manager to own Beamery's Data Foundry end to end. The Data Foundry is our proprietary data platform, powering existing and emerging product lines including our Talent CRM and Workforce Suite. Through this, we provide data-as-a-service to customers through channels such as MCP/API. This is an emerging commercial channel. Its core capabilities span the data models, taxonomies and integrations that underpin talent and workforce decisions across our platform. The Senior Product Manager, Data Foundry will treat data both as infrastructure embedded within our products and as a product that customers buy in its own right. Beyond internal embedding and direct commercial sales, the platform is open — customers and partners can build on top of it through MCP and API access. You will work with product leadership to set the strategy, agree what the platform provides internally, decide what becomes customer-facing, and define how the platform opens up for customer and partner innovation. You will work at the centre of the platform, creating a balance between two essential initiatives. On one side, you serve the Talent CRM and Workforce Suite product managers as your customers, agreeing the data contracts they build on. On the other, you partner with the data science, data engineering and integrations engineering leads to turn those needs into delivery. What you will be doing Ownership and strategy Own the Data Foundry vision, strategy and roadmap, framing each item as a bet with a clear driver, aligned to overall strategic objectives Ensure alignment of Data Foundry strategy to Beamery's AI strategy, reflecting the shift from providing AI assistants to providing AI access through MCP and API channels. Decide what Data Foundry provides as internal infrastructure and what is packaged and sold as a customer-facing product. Make and defend build versus buy decisions across integrations, analytics, AI and taxonomy capabilities. Discovery and commercial impact Discover and validate what external customers want from data-as-a-service, and partner with Sales and Customer Success to drive adoption with clear GTM and enablement plans Build the case for Data Foundry as a new commercial channel, defining and proving the standalone commercial model alongside its role as platform foundation, quantify the value it unlocks for specific customers and deals, and measure success against value and usage metrics. Partnership and delivery Lead your team to deliver solutions our customers can’t imagine working without and that deliver measurable customer and business outcomes Agree and maintain the data contracts with the CRM and Workforce Suite product managers, treating them as internal customers with real commitments. Prioritise across data science, data engineering and integrations engineering, translating tribe needs into a clear and deliverable plan. Communication & alignment Communicate transparently and create alignment between peers and leadership on priorities, trade offs and progress Manage customer and sales expectations through well managed structured cadences Data governance and trust Own how workforce data is governed, secured and access-controlled as it is exposed through APIs and MCP, meeting or exceeding enterprise privacy and compliance expectations. Ensure the outputs of Data Foundry's models are measurable and explainable, so customers and internal teams can trust and act on the results. What we are looking for A product manager with a minimum 6 years experience in complex technical, data or AI products, a significant portion of which should be in enterprise B2B SaaS. Strong grasp of data platforms, APIs and integrations, comfortable making architecture-adjacent decisions while collaborating with and holding priorities with engineering and data science leads. Experience handling sensitive or regulated data, with a clear view of governance, security and privacy. An analytical thinker who uses data to find opportunities, confidently prioritise and measure success, balancing between competing tribe roadmaps and internal customers. Commercially fluent, experience with 0-1 product stages, shaping early product with new go to market motions, able to connect product decisions to revenue, cost and customer ROI. A clear communicator who builds trust across product, data science and engineering, and who is comfortable taking a position and explaining the reasoning. Experienced owning and delivering AI capabilities, with a keen interest in how AI is reshaping the talent and workforce space, and in giving customers trusted, explainable access to their data. Beamery is for Everybody. Diversity and open expression are fundamental to us. We acknowledge the challenges in our industry and strive to develop an inclusive culture where everybody can contribute. We are dedicated to creating an inclusive environment for everyone, regardless of ethnicity, religion, color, sexual orientation, gender identity, race, national origin, age, disability status, or caregiver status. If, for whatever reason, you need us to make reasonable adjustments and adaptations to our recruitment process, please email Visit our Diversity, Equality and Inclusion page to learn more about progress and commitments. title: Chief Medical Officer, UK/I & EMEA
description: Chief Medical Officer, UK/I & EMEA The Role Lyrebird is reshaping how clinical documentation happens across the NHS and in Ireland, and we’re looking for a Chief Medical Officer to be the senior clinical voice of the business. Reporting to the CEO, you’ll make sure everything we build, deploy and sell is clinically safe, evidence-based and genuinely useful to clinicians and patients. You’ll own our clinical safety and governance framework, including DCB0129 and oversight of the Clinical Safety Officer function. You’ll shape the product roadmap alongside Product and Engineering, build the evidence base that NHS and HSE buyers need, and act as a trusted peer to CCIOs, CMIOs, medical directors and ICB leaders. This role suits a practising or recently practising doctor who has led at a senior level in the NHS and knows digital health from the inside. You’re comfortable moving between a board presentation, a hazard log and a conversation with engineers in the same afternoon. You’ll enjoy the pace of a high-growth company, but you’ll never trade safety for speed. title: Senior People Partner
description: Senior People Partner Cloudscaler | London | People Team | Reports to the Chief People Officer | £55,000–£75,000 Someone has to own the People initiative that doesn’t fit neatly into anyone’s week and the case nobody else should be handling. That someone is you — not as an escalation point, but as the person who runs the day-to-day of this function. THE MOMENT Cloudscaler is 130 people today. We’ll be 170 by the end of this year, and roughly double again in 2027. The People function is being built in real time alongside that growth, rather than inherited from someone who left years ago. You’ll be the first hire into the People team. For roughly your first year you’ll be the only People professional alongside the CPO, which means running the whole day-to-day of the function: the hardest casework and initiatives, and the operational core that keeps everything moving. A People Partner is planned to join later in 2027, and at that point the operational administration moves to them. This is also a role built with room to grow. As the team expands beyond that second hire, we expect this role to take on day-to-day operational leadership of the People Partner practice, but that isn’t the shape of it on day one. WHAT MAKES THIS DIFFERENT In most People teams, the senior generalist is just a People Partner with a harder case queue. Here, the difference is ownership, not just difficulty. Complex casework: Rather than simply handling harder cases, you’ll own the most complex cases end to end, with no hand back. People initiatives: Rather than contributing to initiatives someone else drives, you’ll own them from design through to embedding. Decision-making: Rather than escalating ambiguity upward, you’ll make the sensible call and document your reasoning. CPO partnership: Rather than acting in a support role to the CPO, you’ll be an operational partner they can confidently delegate to. To be clear about the level: The CPO still designs the People strategy and the systems architecture. You own how it runs day to day, and you’re trusted to run a whole initiative, not just a case. That is a different job to People Partner, not a bigger version of the same one. THE ROLE You’ll sit in the People team reporting to the Chief People Officer. Three strands make up the job: Casework: The employee relations situations with the most complexity or sensitivity land with you, start to finish. Initiatives: When the CPO needs a piece of work owned (a policy rollout, a wellbeing programme, a piece of the reward or benefits agenda), you take it from design through to something that runs. Operations: Until the People Partner joins, you’ll own payroll and benefits administration, onboarding, screening and security clearances, and keeping Rippling accurate. When the People Partner joins, they’ll report to the CPO. You won’t manage them formally, but you’ll lead their handover, you’ll be the person they come to first, and your judgement will set the standard for how this function operates day to day. WHERE THE ROLE STARTS AND STOPS New roles get vague, so here is the boundary as we see it today. Yours The most complex and sensitive employee relations casework, end to end. Full ownership of People initiatives, from design to embedding. Acting as the CPO’s operational partner on ambiguous or cross-cutting problems. Until the People Partner joins (planned for later in 2027): Payroll and benefits administration, including the monthly payroll cycle in Rippling and Mintago. Pre-onboarding, onboarding and probation. Background screening in Zinc. Security clearance coordination. Rippling data quality, workflows and reporting. Our working groups and committees. Once the People Partner joins: A structured handover of the operational core. Day-to-day guidance for the People Partner. Shared Ashby, which Talent Acquisition owns. You’ll work in it from offer through to start date on every hire until the People Partner joins, and on senior hires after that. Mentoring and supporting the People Partner on their casework and initiatives, once they join. Not yours Recruitment delivery, which sits with Talent Acquisition. The design of the People strategy, the operating model and the systems architecture, which sit with the CPO. Formal line management of the People Partner, who will report to the CPO. THE STACK Rippling: Our single source of truth. Until the People Partner joins you’ll run it day to day, including the monthly payroll cycle, data quality and workflows, and you’ll use its reporting at a level that supports whole initiatives. Zinc: Background screening. You’ll run checks for every new joiner until the People Partner joins, and stay close to the senior and sensitive hires after that. Ashby: Owned by Talent Acquisition. You’ll work in it from offer through to start date on the hires you’re responsible for. Claude: A daily tool here. You’ll use it for casework preparation, drafting policy and communications, and pulling together the analysis behind an initiative. Mintago: Our employee benefits and financial wellbeing platform (pensions, salary sacrifice and financial advice). You’ll administer it and keep enrolment accurate until the People Partner takes it on. WHAT YOU’LL DO Own the hardest casework. You’ll run our most complex and sensitive employee relations cases end to end, with the CPO there to sense-check rather than take over. Own initiatives, not tasks. You’ll take a People initiative from a rough brief to something that’s running and embedded, rather than handing it back once the interesting part is done. Run the operational core. Until the People Partner joins, you’ll own the monthly payroll cycle in Rippling, benefits administration including Mintago, onboarding, background screening and security clearances. Accurate, on time, and documented as you go. Hand it over well. When the People Partner arrives, you’ll give them a working system and a clear handover, then stay the person they come to first and the judgement others in the function measure themselves against. Partner with senior leaders. You’ll be credible with leaders on the most difficult conversations: complex change, capability, and situations without a clean playbook. Use AI properly. You’ll use Claude daily to take time out of your own week, checking anything that touches a decision about a person and owning the outcome. Improve what you find. You’ll spot the gaps in policy, process or practice before anyone else does, and bring the CPO a considered view on the fix, not just the problem. WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE AT 12 MONTHS You’re running the most complex ER cases with confidence, and the CPO isn’t being pulled into them. At least one or two People initiatives have gone from a rough brief to something genuinely embedded, owned by you. Payroll, benefits, onboarding and clearances run accurately and on time, and every process is documented well enough to hand over. You’ve helped shape the People Partner hire, so the handover is ready when they land. Senior leaders treat you as a credible operational partner, not an escalation point. You’ve made and documented sensible calls in genuinely ambiguous situations, and they’ve held up. The CPO can hand you an ambiguous problem and trust it gets shaped properly. WHO WE’RE LOOKING FOR Deep employee relations experience. You’ve run complex disciplinaries, grievances and change situations yourself, and you know exactly when to escalate and when not to. CIPD qualification, or solid progress towards it, is welcome. A track record of owning initiatives. You can point to work you took from a brief to something that actually ran, not just a project you contributed to. Hands-on with the operational detail. You’ve owned or closely supported a payroll cycle, benefits administration and onboarding, and you’re comfortable being accountable for their accuracy while also carrying the senior work. Credible with senior leaders. You can hold your own in a difficult conversation with someone under real pressure and be listened to. Comfortable operating near-autonomously. You don’t need a playbook for everything. You make a sensible call, write it down, and check it with the CPO afterwards. Ready to grow into people leadership. You won’t formally manage anyone at the start, but you’ll induct and guide the People Partner when they join, and you should want to lead a team as the structure catches up. Discreet and organised at volume. Complex casework and live initiatives, often at the same time. You’ll need a system, and it can’t be your memory. THE HONEST PART This role sits in an odd space for now: senior in scope and judgement, without a team underneath it yet. Until the People Partner joins later in 2027, you’ll also be the whole operational team, so a payroll deadline and a complex grievance can land in the same week. That eases as the function grows, but it means the authority you carry day to day has to come from the quality of your work, not a job title. You are not designing the People strategy or the systems architecture. The CPO does that. What you get instead is real ownership of the hardest cases and the initiatives that matter, a close working relationship with the CPO, and a genuine path toward leading the People Partner practice as it grows. This probably isn’t for you if you want a formal team from day one, or if you’d rather leave payroll and onboarding to someone else. It probably is for you if you want to prove you can run this function well enough, top to bottom, that a team gets built around you. If that sounds like the challenge you’ve been looking for, let’s talk. title: General Counsel (Office based)
description: <p>We are hiring a <strong>General Counsel</strong> to lead Canonical’s global Legal and Compliance function and to build the legal architecture a public company needs — commercial contracting, corporate governance, intellectual property and compliance — in a software business that regularly does things the industry has not done before. You will report to the Chief Operating Officer and advise the CEO, CFO and the Board directly.</p> <p><strong>Location</strong>: <strong>Location</strong>: This role can be home-based in EMEA, or office-based in our London, UK office.</p> <h3><strong>About our team</strong></h3> <p>Canonical’s Legal and Compliance function is a distributed team across EMEA and the Americas. It owns the terms on which Ubuntu and our commercial products reach the market: open source and intellectual property licensing, enterprise and channel contracting, data protection, export controls and trade, competition, and the governance a company preparing to list has to be able to evidence.</p> <p>Canonical is founder-led, profitable and growing, and privately held with the intention to list on a public exchange. That makes this a function in transition. The work is as much building the architecture — a management layer across two regions, standard contracting positions, controls, policies and records — as it is advising on live matters, and it is done in a company that regularly does things the industry has not done before, so the precedents often do not exist.</p> <p>The team works with Product and Engineering on licensing and IP, with Security on customer assurance, with Finance on listing readiness and controls, and with Sales on the commitments we make to customers. As General Counsel you lead that team, set its standards, and advise the CEO, COO, CFO and the Board and its committees directly.</p> <h3><strong>What you'll do</strong></h3> <ul> <li>Lead the global Legal and Compliance function: set its structure, standards and priorities across EMEA and the Americas, so the business gets consistent answers wherever it operates.</li> <li>Build the management layer: hire and develop managers, set objectives, review performance against a clear bar, and address under-performance directly rather than waiting it out.</li> <li>Set the operating cadence of the function: how legal work is taken in and prioritised, what internal clients can expect and when, and how workload and risk are reported to the leadership team.</li> <li>Own public-market readiness on the legal side: corporate governance, group and entity structure, delegated authority, policies, disclosure controls and records, in partnership with Finance.</li> <li>Advise the CEO, COO, CFO and the Board, and support Board and committee meetings.</li> <li>Own the commercial contracting framework: standard templates, negotiating positions, and a deviation and escalation process that makes commitments visible before they are signed.</li> <li>Lead intellectual property and open source licensing strategy: permissive and copyleft licences, trademark, and the terms on which Ubuntu and our products are distributed.</li> <li>Own the global compliance programme: data protection and privacy, export controls and trade compliance, anti-bribery and corruption, competition, and AI regulation.</li> <li>Manage litigation, disputes and regulatory engagement, and own the external counsel panel, its budget and the quality of its work.</li> <li>Advise on M&A, partnerships, strategic alliances and financing as the company grows.</li> </ul> <h3><strong>What we are looking for in you</strong></h3> <ul> <li>Qualified as a lawyer, with a law degree or equivalent and an active licence to practise in an EMEA or Americas jurisdiction.</li> <li>In-house legal leadership in a software or technology company — a business that licenses its own products, rather than one that buys technology to run its operations.</li> <li>Commercial technology contracting: enterprise software and subscription agreements, channel and reseller agreements, cloud and services, and hardware manufacturer agreements.</li> <li>Open source licensing: permissive and copyleft licences, trademark, and how open source communities work in practice.</li> <li>Corporate governance for a listed company, or for one preparing to list: board and committee support, delegated authority, disclosure and controls.</li> <li>Depth in at least two of: data protection and privacy, IP and trademark, export controls and trade, competition, or disputes.</li> <li>Leading a distributed legal team, including managing managers across regions and time zones.</li> <li>Building or restructuring an in-house legal function, including deciding what is retained, delegated and sent to external counsel.</li> <li>A track record of setting and holding a high performance bar: hiring well, developing people, and dealing with under-performance directly rather than waiting it out.</li> <li>An exceptional academic track record from both high school and university.</li> <li>Professional written and spoken English, with excellent drafting and presentation skills.</li> <li>Ability to travel internationally two to four times a year, for company events up to two weeks long.</li> </ul> <h3><strong>Nice-to-have skills</strong></h3> <ul> <li>Experience taking a company through an IPO, or practising as counsel inside a listed company.</li> <li>A technical or engineering background, or fluency in how software is built and shipped.</li> <li>Experience of a subscription or recurring-revenue business model.</li> <li>A qualification in more than one jurisdiction.</li> </ul> <p><strong>How we work</strong></p> <p>We look for a track record of going above-and-beyond expectations to achieve outstanding results, backed by self-motivation and drive. Our people deliver their work precisely, taking care to deliver correctness and clarity. Reliability is at our core, where colleagues deliver high quality work that builds trust and confidence. We make ourselves accessible, collaborating to build products and systems that are usable. Finally we are adroit, blending enthusiasm, knowledge, adaptability, style and character.</p> <h3><strong>What we offer colleagues</strong></h3> <p>We consider geographical location, experience, and performance in shaping compensation worldwide. We revisit compensation annually (and more often for graduates and associates) to ensure we recognize outstanding performance. In addition to base pay, we offer a performance-driven annual bonus or commission. We provide all team members with additional benefits which reflect our values and ideals. We balance our programs to meet local needs and ensure fairness globally.</p> <ul> <li>Distributed work environment with twice-yearly team sprints in person.</li> <li>Personal learning and development budget of USD 2,000 per year.</li> <li>Bi-annual compensation review.</li> <li>Company recognition rewards.</li> <li>40 days annual leave per annum, including public holidays and our All Company holiday periods.</li> <li>Maternity and paternity leave.</li> <li>Team Member Assistance Program & Wellness Platform.</li> <li>Opportunity to travel to new locations to meet colleagues, with Priority Pass for lounge access.</li> </ul> <h3><strong>About Canonical</strong></h3> <p>Canonical is a pioneering tech firm at the forefront of the global move to open source. Our platform, Ubuntu, is very widely used in breakthrough enterprise initiatives such as public cloud, data science, AI, engineering innovation, and IoT. Our customers include the world's leading public cloud and silicon providers, and industry leaders in many sectors. We are founder-led, profitable, and growing.</p> <p>Powered by worldwide distributed collaboration since our inception in 2004, we believe tech and business leadership can emerge anywhere. We have no central headquarters. Most of us work from home, but we are exceptionally disciplined about this. We have very high expectations of all colleagues, and are champions of excellence. Working here is a step into the future and will challenge you to think differently, work smarter, learn new skills, and raise your game.</p> <p><strong>Canonical is an equal opportunity employer</strong></p> <p>We are proud to foster a workplace free from discrimination. Diversity of experience, perspectives, and background create a better work environment and better products.<a href="https://canonical.com/careers/diversity/identity"> Whatever your identity, we will give your application fair consideration.</a></p>

title: Senior Copywriter
description: <div class="content-intro"><h3><strong>Who We Are</strong></h3> <p>VML is a global creative company that combines brand experience, customer experience, and commerce to create connected brands that drive growth. Guided by a <strong>Human First</strong> philosophy, VML is known for its innovative work for brands and consistently ranks among the world’s leading creative companies, including the WARC Creative 100. VML’s global network spans 55+ markets with principal offices in Buenos Aires, Kansas City, London, New York, São Paulo, Shanghai and Singapore. </p> <p>VML is part of WPP, the trusted growth partner for the world's leading brands. Powered by exceptional talent and our agentic marketing platform WPP Open, WPP unites cutting-edge media intelligence and data solutions, creativity, production, enterprise solutions and expert strategic counsel. </p> <p>For more information, please visit <a href="http://www.vml.com/" data-outlook-id="d4b7d1c3-8ad6-4b6d-ab45-d3cb5a3aebe1">www.vml.com </a>and follow along on <a href="https://urldefense.proofpoint.com/v2/url?u=https-3A__urldefense.com_v3_-5F-5Fhttps-3A_www.linkedin.com_company_vml_-5F-5F-3B-21-21JboVxjCXSME-21OhlpCfbkl1UcWPwns1-2DGtvHOzFh0QwHV49fsPgGw-2DVCCU1bCg8aQFI9vN-2Dy-2DVwaQcITH2j2XKzGKBIFRLYf2AUWVYY1dFGK6-24&d=DwMFaQ&c=euGZstcaTDllvimEN8b7jXrwqOf-v5A_CdpgnVfiiMM&r=zouFnm4jZMgDFaYF1uVcRY3rbgHWPca_luUrBUkT6Yc&m=QzcCgXCAOjzj5hiU48_CKOdHRSJ4_YpuqfviT9yjlzH5VrkzySTZ-WaQXlYAnj4W&s=jJ7q5V70u9oUx7ONPm5jC3IK8y6vxDilX6BGTlqlWlA&e=" data-outlook-id="a3ef68bf-16fb-4ebc-9ca9-406007d6cefc">LinkedIn</a> #WeAreVML.</p></div><p><strong>Company: </strong><strong>VML</strong></p> <p><strong>Working Model: </strong><strong>Hybrid working</strong></p> <p><strong>Location: </strong><strong>Sea Containers office, London, SE1</strong></p> <p>At VML, we are a beacon of innovation and growth in an ever-evolving world. Our heritage is built upon a century of combined expertise, where creativity meets technology, and diverse perspectives ignite inspiration. With the merger of VMLY&R and Wunderman Thompson, we have forged a new path as a growth partner that is part creative agency, part consultancy, and part technology powerhouse.</p> <p>Our global family now encompasses over 30,000 employees across 150+ offices in 64 markets, each contributing to a culture that values connection, belonging, and the power of differences. Our expertise spans the entire customer journey building connected brands that drive growth for our clients. We do this by leveraging our 3 core practices; Brand experience, Customer experience and Commerce. Within these practices we offer expertise across communications, commerce, consultancy, CRM, data, production, and technology. We deliver end-to-end solutions that result in revolutionary work.</p> <p><strong>The Role: Senior Copywriter</strong></p> <p>We’re looking for a senior writer, to work on one of the world’s leading car groups – covering a range of brands on their roster.</p> <p>The ideal candidate needs to be a conceptually sound creative with a history of big ideas. A specialist in copywriting who has worked through the line, and is not afraid to get stuck in at the lower end of the funnel.</p> <p>The day-to-day ask is to work on developing standout copy for a range of CRM communications – Direct Mail, Email, SMS, MMS and digital & social.</p> <p>Beyond that you will have creative opportunities to expand your thinking across other mediums, being more conceptual, as we look to expand the brands beyond CRM.</p> <p>The ideal candidate will be experienced in creating compelling content that elevates engagement, enhances customer loyalty, and drives business revenue. We're a 160+ person team - operators, data scientists, engineers, customer champions and energy experts - backed by top-tier investors including Lightspeed Venture Partners, Hitachi Ventures, Allianz, AlbionVC and Atomico. We closed a $75M Series B round in early 2026, taking our total funding to $94M, and we now power energy for over 4,000 UK businesses across 8,500+ sites , with over £75m in value returned to businesses and generators so far. We're a technology company solving the energy industry, not an energy company. Some people call us a neo-utility, the neo-bank idea, applied to energy. The industry is noticing. We were crowned Europe's Most Exciting Tech Company at the GP Bullhound Allstars awards , came in at #6 on LinkedIn's Top Startups 2026 in the UK, #7 on the Scaling Europe 50 of Europe's fastest-growing companies, and #14 on Sifted's AI 100 . Learn more about us on our website . 🚀 The Role We're hiring a People Performance Manager to join our Performance Service. tem is growing fast. Our goal is to get better as we get bigger - revenue growing faster than headcount. In practice that means keeping our strongest people engaged and performing, getting new joiners productive quickly, and enabling our leaders to multiply their impact over time. Most companies solve that with layers of management. We don't. Our leaders (Player-Coaches) coach their teams while staying hands-on with the work, which means the systems around them have to do more of the lifting. That's where the Performance Service comes in. We're a team of four, and we own how tem runs as an organisation: the operating rhythm (how work gets planned, tracked, escalated and reported), the onboarding and development that build capability, the frameworks that define what good performance looks like and how people progress and get paid, and the operational backbone of contracts, benefits and payroll. We don't own recruitment. We're adding a second Performance Partner because we need more hands on deck - both partnering with our leaders day to day, and building the frameworks that support them. Your patch is sustained performance - the part that runs continuously once someone is through the door. You'll carry a portfolio of leaders across our Engines and Services that you're accountable for, and you'll co-own the frameworks that sit underneath them alongside the rest of the team. You will not be handed a finished playbook to administer. You'll report into the Performance Service Manager. HR experience is welcome but not required - we're open to operators, people who've led teams, and the sort of person who ends up owning whatever the company needs next. In your first 12 months, you might: Become the first call for a portfolio of leaders on anything to do with their people - performance calls, team decisions and hard conversations. Co-design how progression, performance standards, evaluation and reward actually work at tem, alongside the rest of the Performance team. Handle live cases end to end - performance management, difficult conversations, exits and restructures. Use AI and automation so the operational layer runs itself and your time goes on judgement, not process. Turn recurring employee and manager pain points into better processes, tools, guidance or self-service, and measure whether they work. 🛠️ Responsibilities Coach and challenge: be a leader's first call on anything to do with their people - a decision they want a second view on, coaching on how to handle a situation, or a read on employment law - and hold a position when you disagree with them. Raise the bar: hold leaders to a high standard on performance, potential, pay and progression - help them make sharper calls, and hold consistency across your patch. Handle live cases end to end: performance management, difficult conversations, exits and restructures. Build to delight: shape how progression, performance standards, evaluation and reward actually work at tem, alongside the rest of the Performance team. We treat our people like top athletes, and our aim is to delight them at every step of their employee experience - the systems around them have to express that at every contact point. Design for our shape, not the textbook: we index on outcomes and impact in everything - how progression works, how teams are structured, what leaders spend their time on. Most standard people frameworks assume a management hierarchy we don't have. Automate the repeatable: use AI and automation so the operational layer runs itself and your time goes on judgement, not process. Think in process, scalability and iteration: turn recurring employee and manager pain points into better processes, tools, guidance or self-service. Measure whether they work and redesign when they don't fit the purpose. ✅ Requirements You do not need a CIPD qualification, and you do not need to have worked in a large, established HR function. You might have been a founder's associate or Chief of Staff at a Series A or B startup, holding the place together while it scaled. You might have built a People function from scratch and taken it from a one-person band to a well-oiled machine. You might have run a team or an Operations function where the people calls were effectively yours, even if People or HR never appeared in your job title. Or you might have done a different job that helped you build the skills below. A background in HR might help you do this job well, but it is not a requirement. Must-Haves You've held real accountability for decisions on people - you've partnered with leaders, or managed a team yourself, where hiring, performance and exit calls were either yours or made on your guidance. You can be trusted with the hardest conversations in the business and you're recognised for how you handle them, and you understand how decisions about people shape culture and employer brand - balancing efficiency with empathy. You've worked in or towards building a high-performance culture, and you're a confident challenger who carries conviction and can influence leadership decisions. You're comfortable operating without a playbook, in a company where the requirements and the shape of your role change constantly. You think from first principles, get to the root cause of complex problems, weigh competing considerations and anticipate second-order consequences. You're fluent with Notion, automation and AI tooling - your instinct is to build the thing rather than do it manually a second time - and you write clearly enough that a busy person reads it once and comes away with a clear idea of the situation and the next actions. Desirable Employment relations experience in the UK, Europe or the US - we operate across the UK and Europe today, with plans to expand to the US soon. Experience working across multiple countries, including employer of record arrangements. Compensation and benchmarking experience - salary banding, pay review cycles, market data. 🎁 Benefits & Perks Stock options so everyone has ownership in our mission. 25 days holiday plus public holidays. Swap public holidays for the ones that matter most to you, and enjoy your birthday off. Remote first and flexible working, with clear core hours and no internal meetings on Friday afternoons. Up to GBP1,200 or EUR1,400 per year for your remote setup. Up to GBP150 or EUR170 per month for wellbeing. 🤝 Interview Process We move fast. Most processes take 2 to 3 weeks from first chat to offer. If you need us to adapt anything, let us know. Intro call with our Talent team. Skills interview, which might include a practical exercise we may ask you to prepare in advance. Hiring Manager interview. Bar Raiser interview with leadership stakeholders. We welcome applications from people of all backgrounds, experiences, and identities, including those that are traditionally underrepresented in the tech and energy sectors. If you’re excited about this role but not sure you meet every requirement, we’d still love to hear from you. Your unique perspective could be exactly what we’re looking for.
